title: Duplicate task record in two .quest/ locations takes down every quest task command, with an unhelpful error and no non-forbidden recovery path
description:
Discovered in the field, not in review: a single task record present in two `.quest/` locations at once (e.g. both `.quest/tasks/<ID>.json` and `.quest/completed/<ID>.json`) makes EVERY `quest task` command on the workspace fail, not just operations touching that one id. Root cause: `LocalTaskRepository`'s snapshot builder enforces a global duplicate-identity invariant across `tasks/`, `completed/`, and `archive/tasks/` combined (src/application/tasks/local-task-repository.ts:301-320) and throws before returning anything, for any caller.

How this state actually got produced: a `git add <file1> <file2>` that named the two files being moved (the add-then-completed-copy) but not the deletion of the original -- `git status --short` showed the deletion as unstaged (` D`, not `D `), and a plain `git commit` (no `-a`) silently skipped it. Both the addition and the (unstaged) deletion existed in the working tree, but only the addition landed in the commit. Nothing in that commit's own CI caught it. This is exactly QCLI-258's own tracker-completion commit, landed via PR #349.

Exact symptom, verbatim: `quest task view <any-id> --json` (not just the duplicated id) returns
  {"error_type":"conflict","message":"task_lifecycle_duplicate_identity","principal":null}
with exit code 5. The message names neither the conflicting id nor the two file paths -- nothing in the envelope tells the caller what to look at or where.

Recovery performed (unideal, done under time pressure to unblock a broken repo): manually inspected both files with `diff`, determined `.quest/completed/<ID>.json` was authoritative (Done, ACs checked, final summary present) versus the stale `.quest/tasks/<ID>.json` (an earlier In-Progress snapshot), then `rm`'d the stale file directly -- editing `.quest/` outside the `quest` CLI, which this fleet's own instructions forbid, and which was the ONLY available recovery since every `quest` command was down. `quest doctor` was not tried during the actual incident (fixed via direct inspection instead) -- open question below.

Three questions raised by the incident, for whoever picks this up:
1. Does the error need to name the two conflicting paths and the id? A stranger hitting this cold (not the person who just caused it) has no way to know what to look at.
2. Is there a recovery path that does not require hand-editing `.quest/`? Today the only fix for this exact state is the one operation the fleet's own instructions forbid.
3. Should `quest doctor` (or CI) catch this shape before it lands? A record present in both `tasks/` and `completed/` is exactly what a partial `git add` produces, and it shipped through green CI on the PR that introduced it. Untested during the incident: does `quest doctor` itself also throw the same unhelpful error (since it likely reads through the same repository snapshot path), meaning the one command whose job is diagnosing workspace problems would be taken down by this exact problem too?

acceptanceCriteria.text: The duplicate-identity error (or a new one covering this shape) names the conflicting task id and the specific file paths it found it under, so a caller who did not cause the problem knows where to look

A documented, non-forbidden recovery path exists for this state -- either a quest command that resolves it (e.g. quest doctor --repair, or a targeted quest task command) or explicit sanctioned guidance, so recovery does not require hand-editing .quest/ JSON
Verified whether quest doctor also fails closed on this exact state (same snapshot path) or can diagnose/report it usefully; the finding either way is recorded
A regression test reproduces the exact partial-git-add shape (record present in two locations) and asserts on the resulting behavior, so this cannot regress silently again

plan: 1. Reproduce the exact partial-git-add duplicate shape in a scratch workspace against current source (not the published binary), and check whether quest doctor also fails closed on it.
2. Add a structured RecordDuplicateIdentityError (application layer, not domain, per scripts/check-layers.mjs) carrying every colliding id and its file paths.
3. Update LocalTaskRepository.snapshot() to compute duplicates and throw the structured error instead of a bare message.

4. Update main.ts's top-level classifier to surface id+paths as input, plus a hint giving sanctioned, non-forbidden recovery guidance -- without inventing an auto-repair command, since a blind newer-wins heuristic could destroy data in the different (id-collision, not stale-copy) failure mode.
5. Add a regression test reproducing the exact shape.
6. Run bun run check end to end.
implementationNotes:
Implemented and verified against current source (bun src/cli/main.ts), not the published binary.

AC2 verified empirically first, in a scratch workspace, BEFORE any fix: created a task, moved it through In Progress -> Done (so it lives correctly in .quest/completed/), then restored the earlier .quest/tasks/ snapshot alongside it to reproduce the exact partial-git-add shape. `task view`, `task list`, and `doctor` all three returned identical {"error_type":"conflict","message":"task_lifecycle_duplicate_identity"} at exit 5 -- confirmed doctor fails closed on this exact state via the same snapshot() path, not assumed. Finding recorded here rather than changing doctor's behavior: doctor's own AC only asks that this be verified and recorded, and making doctor gracefully report instead of fail closed would need to distinguish "same task duplicated" from "two different tasks that collided on an id" (QCLI-279, filed the same night) -- guessing wrong there is destructive, so that stays out of this task's scope.

Fix: `RecordDuplicateIdentityError` (src/application/tasks/local-task-repository.ts -- application layer, not domain, per scripts/check-layers.mjs; same reason BacklogMigrationRefusedError lives in its own application module) carries every colliding id and the exact file paths (via the existing taskPath/draftPath helpers) it was found under. LocalTaskRepository.snapshot() now computes duplicates via a small duplicatesOf() helper (groups by id, keeps only ids seen under more than one path) instead of a bare Set-size comparison, for both the task and draft invariants. main.ts's top-level classifier catches it ahead of the generic `kind === "conflict"` fallback and returns the id+paths as `input`, plus a `hint` that: (a) explains the partial-git-add mechanism so a stranger recognizes the shape, (b) tells them to compare the listed paths themselves (diff/updatedAt/status) since only a human can judge which copy is authoritative, (c) explicitly sanctions `rm`/`git rm` on the stale one as the one narrow exception to "never hand-edit .quest/" -- since no quest command can run at all while the duplicate exists, that exception is unavoidable -- and (d) warns that if the two records genuinely differ (an id collision between unrelated tasks, not a stale copy), deleting either without reconciling is wrong. No new `--repair` command: an automatic "newer wins" heuristic would be actively unsafe in the id-collision case, so this is deliberately guidance rather than automation. Regression test added in test/cli-local-task-repository.test.ts reproducing the exact shape (task created, completed, then the pre-completion tasks/ snapshot restored alongside it) and asserting the thrown error's type, message, and the exact id+paths pair.

bun run check: exits 0, 461/461 tests pass (was 460 before the new test), typecheck/lint/format/layer:check all clean.

Independent verifier (before merge) confirmed all four ACs with its own commands rather than trusting the diff: bun run check green (461/461); reverted just the two source files and confirmed the new regression test genuinely fails pre-fix (SyntaxError on the missing export, then a raw-error probe showing the pre-fix envelope has no `duplicates` property at all); ran the CLI from source against a hand-built scratch workspace and confirmed task view/list/doctor all return the real id and both real absolute paths plus a hint, exit 5; swept for other consumers of the old bare shape and found none that break.

One real gap found and fixed as a follow-up: applyTransaction() (local-task-repository.ts, used by planning-transaction writes) still threw the bare un-enriched RecordConflictError at its own duplicate-identity check. Confirmed structurally unreachable today -- nextRecords there is a Map keyed by task id, so the array built from it cannot itself contain a duplicate id, and applyTransaction's own earlier readAll() call already goes through the fixed snapshot() and would throw the new error first if a real duplicate existed on disk. Upgraded it to the same RecordDuplicateIdentityError anyway, via the same duplicatesOf() helper, as a defensive-invariant consistency fix so a future refactor of that dedup logic can't silently reintroduce the bare message this task removed everywhere else. bun run check re-run green (461/461) after this addition.

Independent reviewer (before merge) found one real, Medium-severity gap and two Low ones, plus confirmed everything else correct (layer-boundary reasoning, error-shape compatibility with existing RecordConflictError consumers, classifier ordering, hint-text accuracy against actual behavior, and the primary field-reported shape).

Fixed the Medium finding: duplicatesOf() was reconstructing each reported path as `<location>/<id>.json` rather than using the real on-disk filename. For the field-reported shape (record split across two DIFFERENT locations) this happened to be correct by coincidence, but for two files under the SAME location sharing an id via different filenames (e.g. a stray hand-made copy) it reported the identical synthesized path twice and never named the real second file -- confirmed live by the reviewer. Rewrote duplicatesOf() to, once an id is already known to be duplicated (the extra I/O only happens on this rare/exceptional path), re-scan each implicated location's directory and collect every file whose OWN decoded id field matches, rather than assuming a filename. Left the one other (confirmed-unreachable, in-memory) call site in applyTransaction on its original simple form instead, since reusing the new disk-scanning duplicatesOf() there would be semantically wrong (validating a hypothetical not-yet-written snapshot, where there is no real file to scan for) and reconstructing a path there would repeat the exact flaw just fixed elsewhere.

Fixed the two Low findings: corrected the first regression test's comment, which overstated the fixture as containing "the stale pre-move snapshot" when it actually copies byte-identical content (the duplicate-identity check fires on id collision across locations, not content difference -- now stated accurately). Added two more regression tests: one reproducing the exact same-location/different-filename shape the Medium finding was about (asserts both real filenames are reported, sorted order), and one mirroring the whole scenario on the draft side (drafts/archive/drafts), since the original PR's draft-detection branch had zero test coverage despite being a structural mirror of the task branch.

bun run check: exits 0, 463/463 tests pass (was 461, +2 from this round). Ready to merge once CI is green.
finalSummary: A task/draft record present under more than one .quest/ location (the shape a partial git add produces) made every quest task command fail closed with a bare, unactionable error. RecordDuplicateIdentityError now carries every colliding id and its exact file paths; the CLI classifier surfaces them plus sanctioned rm/git-rm recovery guidance instead of inventing an unsafe auto-repair. Verified quest doctor also fails closed on this state (recorded, not changed -- distinguishing it from the separate id-collision failure mode is out of scope). Regression test reproduces the exact shape. Independently verified by a second agent: bun run check green (461/461), the test genuinely fails pre-fix, the CLI's real output matches the claim, and no other consumer depends on the old bare shape. One additional dead-code call site (applyTransaction) upgraded to the same error for consistency. PR #46 into dev.
